sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from $22.7 billion in FY2016 to $31.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F9][F198].
Operating income grew faster at 5.8% a year [F199], and net income faster still at 9.7% [F200].
Operating income fell 19.9% in FY2020, cutting operating margin 3.8pp to 19.7%, on impairment charges from the coal ash CCR settlement and COVID-19 volume losses [D156][D168][F23][P53][P60].
Net income rose 59.2% to $4.52 billion in FY2024, primarily because the prior year carried higher impairments on the Commercial Renewables sale [D320][F37][P18].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 3.6pp of FY2025's 5.6% revenue growth and made up 90.9% of revenue [D543][D358][D541].
Residential electric added 2.8pp, and Gas Utilities and Infrastructure added 2.0pp as Piedmont Natural Gas revenue rose 32.1% [D776][D566][D517].
The filing passages in the pack do not state a cause for the FY2025 segment revenue gains.
Operating income grew 8.8% against 5.6% revenue growth in FY2025, an incremental operating margin of 41.4% [D359][D358][D378].
Diluted shares rose from 691.0 million to 777.0 million, so EPS compounded at 8.2% against 9.7% for net income [X106][X115][F201][F200].
FY2025 operating margin of 27.2% is the window high, above the 22.9% median and the 19.7% low [F28][D932][D933][D931].
That sits at the 75th percentile of four utility peers, whose median operating margin is 25.7% [D949][D950].
Operating expenses grew 5.3% against revenue growth of 5.6%, which lifted operating margin 0.8pp in FY2025 [D372][D358][D370].
Depreciation and amortization rose to 24.3% of revenue in FY2025 from 21.4% in FY2024 [D341][D303].
Interest expense reached $3.38 billion in FY2024, primarily on higher debt balances and interest rates [X62][P9].
FY2025 operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income, yet capex of $14.0 billion left free cash flow at -$1.69 billion [F77][D346][F87][F97].
Capex ran at 44.2% of revenue and 1.82x D&A, and free cash flow margin of -5.3% compares with a -5.8% window median [D342][D348][D343][D939].
FY2022 free cash flow of -$5.44 billion followed undercollected fuel costs, financed by increased borrowings [F94][P36].
Net debt reached $89.6 billion in FY2025, up from $84.0 billion a year earlier [D352][D314].
Net cash was -282.3% of revenue, at the 25th percentile of four utility peers whose median is -228.4% [D353][D953][D954].
Debt issued of $11.9 billion was more than double the $5.65 billion repaid in FY2025, and diluted shares rose 0.6% [X133][X143][D374].
Return on average equity of 9.7% is at the 0th percentile of four peers, against a 12.6% median [D357][D955][D956].
Liquidity is thin: the current ratio was 0.55x against a window low of 0.53x, and cash of $245 million covers 0.1 years of burn [R1][F177][D943][R2][F137][D356].
Current portion of debt rose to $7.10 billion from $4.35 billion, so continued access to debt markets matters for this ratio [X160][X159].
Net debt rose nine years in a row, from $50.0 billion in FY2016 to $89.6 billion, while interest expense went from $1.92 billion to $3.63 billion [R3][D14][D352][X54][X63].
Free cash flow was -0.34x net income in FY2025, against a -0.62x window median, and only FY2024 came near breakeven at 0.01x [R4][D347][D942][D309].

Receivables fell to $16 million in FY2025 from $1.89 billion, implying 0 days of sales outstanding, and the cited filings do not explain it, so working-capital comparisons across that break are unreliable [X190][X189][D354].
A current ratio below the window low of 0.53x, from 0.55x now, would confirm the liquidity strain in the FY2026 10-K [D943][F177].
Revenue growth minus operating-cost growth turning negative from +0.3pp would reverse the operating leverage story in the FY2026 10-K [D379].
A free cash flow margin above the window high of 0.2%, from -5.3%, would show capex funded internally in the FY2026 10-K [D938][D343].
